item.title: Datec outlines Kina-backed expansion plans
item.description: Datec PNG is embarking on a major expansion into new age Information Communication Technology [ICT] services, extending its operations across the country and into the Pacific region. Datec PNG chief executive officer Preetam Talukdar revealed the expansion plans during the launching of the company's new showroom in Lae, Morobe.
item.content:encoded:
Datec PNG is embarking on a major expansion into new age Information Communication Technology [ICT] services, extending its operations across the country and into the Pacific region.

Datec PNG chief executive officer Preetam Talukdar revealed the expansion plans during the launching of the company's new showroom in Lae, Morobe.

Talukdar said Datec PNG remains the largest ICT solutions and service provider in the country, currently employing 250 Papua New Guineans.

"We are decentralising to Mt Hagen, and will extend our services to Honiara (Solomon Islands), and open another commercial building opposite APEC Haus this year," Talukdar said.

"We will then also upgrade our branches in Wewak, Rabaul and Alotau by next year. As we extend to those parts of the country, we are going to increase the number of our employees to 500 by the end of next year."

Talukdar also confirmed that the company plans to establish its own charity foundation to support community initiatives in centers where it operates.

Datec PNG is a subsidiary of state-owned telecommunications provider Telikom PNG. Established in 1986, Datec originally started operations at the Lae Papuan Compound as a subsidiary of Steamships Trading Company before its acquisition by Telikom.

Telikom PNG chairman Shedrick Sendeke assured the people of Lae of the quality, reliability, and relevance of the technology services being offered.

Sendeke said Datec's return to Lae was a homecoming, but on a much larger scale with advanced technological standards designed to keep local businesses and residents connected.

"Returning to Lae is like returning to our origin, so it is not a new location, but on a bigger scale and advanced technology standard service given to the people, so they are not left behind in the newest technology," Sendeke said.

Meanwhile, Talukdar said the official public opening date for the Lae showroom will be announced soon.

Once open, customers in Lae will gain access to the latest IT consumables, consumer electronics, and Artificial Intelligence [AI] integrated products.

item.title: Basil explains K50,000 school project grants
item.description: Bulolo MP Sam Basil Jnr has clarified the funding mechanism behind the construction of a new classroom at Malangta Primary School in Watut, Morobe, following public criticism surrounding the project’s cost and standard. The opening of the building recently drew widespread criticism on social media, with members of the public questioning the overall value and quality of the facility.
item.content:encoded:
Bulolo MP Sam Basil Jnr has clarified the funding mechanism behind the construction of a new classroom at Malangta Primary School in Watut, Morobe, following public criticism surrounding the project’s cost and standard.

The opening of the building recently drew widespread criticism on social media, with members of the public questioning the overall value and quality of the facility.

Speaking in response to the public reaction, Basil said Malangta Primary was among 33 schools across the district that each received a K50,000 grant from the Bulolo District Development Authority [BDDA] to assist with classroom construction.

"The Bulolo Development Authority, as guided by the Bulolo District Development Plan 2023-2027 under infrastructure support, has provided counter funding which is understood to complement funding obtained from the project component of the Government tuition fee subsidy grants," Basil told NBC News.

"The Bulolo Development Authority provided K50,000 in counter funding to 33 schools right across the district, totalling K1,650,000."

Basil said the funding assistance was never meant to cover the total cost of any single building, but was allocated as financial assistance to aid school boards in delivering their own projects, preferably a two-in-one classroom structure.

He said in addition to the cash grants, the BDDA also supplied 100 sheets of roofing iron to each of the 33 recipient schools.

"This support also reduced construction costs and helped schools complete the classroom projects," Basil said.

"Schools were encouraged to source their own timber and contractor, which basically left the school management boards and their administration to take ownership of the funding and deliver an infrastructure project for their school.

"This meant the school management boards and their administration were responsible for deciding how the funds were used, whether to build through community labour, engage carpenters, or award contracts to a contractor. The designs of the classroom projects were also the prerogative of each school."

Basil further clarified that the district administration had no direct involvement in the execution, design, or management of the building works once the funds and roofing sheets were handed over.

According to figures confirmed by the Bulolo District Education Services; five schools have completed, launched, and acquitted their projects, 28 schools have commenced construction and are nearing completion, and, two schools have yet to begin construction.

"The five schools that have completed and launched their classroom project have also fully acquitted for the funding that they have received, and the Office of the Bulolo DDA Chairman and the Bulolo administration are in receipt of the acquittal," Basil said.

He maintained that the BDDA treated every school in the district equally and would not interfere in the internal decisions of local school boards.

"BDDA don’t micromanage. We are not architects or engineers. We have 33 schools, all receive the same," Basil said.

"It’s not always the role of the DDA to do what we did. They should be happy something is better than nothing. There were no special treatment. We treated all 33 schools the same."

item.title: Koroba people told to protect water sources amid El Niño impacts
item.description: The Koroba Lake Kopiago District Development Authority [KLK DDA] is urging communities across the district to protect remaining water sources as severe El Niño conditions take hold, causing widespread water scarcity across the region. DDA chief executive officer Stanley Kotange issued a critical warning to the people to safeguard local water sources against pollution.
item.content:encoded:
The Koroba Lake Kopiago District Development Authority [KLK DDA] is urging communities across the district to protect remaining water sources as severe El Niño conditions take hold, causing widespread water scarcity across the region.

DDA chief executive officer Stanley Kotange issued a critical warning to the people to safeguard local water sources against pollution.

With smaller creeks and local streams having completely dried up, community members are increasingly relying on major waterways, including the Tagali and Nakia rivers, as well as small lakes and marshland areas.

​"During this extreme El Niño period, I strongly encourage people to fetch water using buckets and carry out their washing and laundry away from the primary source," Kotange said.

"Water must not be contaminated, as communities downstream and nearby rely on these exact same sources for survival. Water is becoming extremely scarce, and a food shortage will inevitably follow. We must preserve and manage whatever resources we currently have available."

​The warning comes following a recent meeting convened by the Hela Provincial Disaster Committee. District Development Authorities across the province have been directed to immediately establish local District Disaster Committees, conduct widespread public awareness campaigns, and submit detailed reports outlining immediate emergency response plans.

​Kotange confirmed that extensive public awareness campaigns are already underway across the district, carried out with operational support from the Koroba Police and members of Mobile Squad 22 [MS22].

In addition to water conservation, authorities are addressing public health hazards linked to the prolonged dry spell. Kotange urged the people to avoid loitering and gambling along roadsides, noting that heavy dust conditions pose serious respiratory health risks.

​"People sitting idle along the roadsides need to stop and return to their homes or gardens," he said. "The roads are heavily coated in dust, creating a high risk of respiratory illness from airborne dust particles."

​Concurrently, law enforcement is cracking down on harmful, non-sustainable harvesting practices. MS22 Commander Jonathan Lakaio issued a stern directive against the use of traditional fish-poisoning techniques, such as crushed tree trunks and toxic bark, in local waterways, warning that violators will face immediate arrest.

​"Using traditional plant toxins will completely wipe out local aquatic life," Commander Lakaio warned. "This is a serious matter. We urge community leaders and ward councilors to spread this message so that our rivers remain clean and our fish populations are not exterminated."

item.title: Behori clan restrained over pipeline blockade
item.description: The National Court yesterday issued urgent restraining orders against members of the Behori clan, preventing further obstruction of Water PNG’s access to the Sogeri pipeline in the Lower Koiari area. Justice Thomas Anis ruled in favor of Water PNG’s application, emphasizing that the city’s population must not be placed at risk by continued blockades.
item.content:encoded:
The National Court yesterday issued urgent restraining orders against members of the Behori clan, preventing further obstruction of Water PNG’s access to the Sogeri pipeline in the Lower Koiari area.

Justice Thomas Anis ruled in favor of Water PNG’s application, emphasizing that the city’s population must not be placed at risk by continued blockades.

The Court’s orders prohibit the Behori clan from blocking, threatening, or harassing Water PNG staff, and from damaging any part of the Sirinumu Dam or water infrastructure.

Water PNG’s Lawyer Edwin Lako said these orders are necessary to safeguard Port Moresby’s water supply and ensure hospitals, schools, and businesses can continue operating without disruption.

The Court confirmed the orders remain in force until further notice, with the matter returning on 17 August 2026.

The dispute arose late July when Behori landowners erected blockades demanding K5.5 million in compensation and reparations.

The obstruction delayed emergency repairs planned with support from Australia, the UN, and other partners, raising fears of rationing and disruption to essential services.

Water PNG welcomes the Court’s swift intervention, noting that uninterrupted access to the pipeline is critical to maintaining public health, safety, and economic stability in the capital.

item.title: Treasurer assists Madang school with K400,000 funding
item.description: Madang Governor Ramsey Pariwa has acknowledged Treasurer Ian Ling-Stuckey for providing K400,000 in financial assistance to Ambarina Primary School in the Ambenob local level government [LLG] area. Governor Pariwa presented a dummy cheque on behalf of the Treasurer to school headmistress Loma Dau during a official ceremony on Friday.
item.content:encoded:
Madang Governor Ramsey Pariwa has acknowledged Treasurer Ian Ling-Stuckey for providing K400,000 in financial assistance to Ambarina Primary School in the Ambenob local level government [LLG] area.

Governor Pariwa presented a dummy cheque on behalf of the Treasurer to school headmistress Loma Dau during a official ceremony on Friday.

The presentation was witnessed by provincial executive council education chairman Gary Kulonga, Ambenob LLG president Dum Bal, and provincial education director Alphonse Igag.

Pariwa explained that the funding fulfilled a pledge originally made by Ling-Stuckey, who is also the Member for Kavieng, when he backed the construction of the school's administration block in 2023.

The completed administration facility now houses a staff room, computer lab, and printing setup for the school.

Pariwa said that he persistently reminded the Treasurer to honor his original K100,000 commitment during annual provincial budget presentations in 2023, 2024, and 2025.

He said he challenged the Treasurer to add K100,000 for every year the pledge remained outstanding, eventually boosting the final payout to K400,000.

“We must have a strategy, don't become an ordinary leader,” Pariwa said. “We have to be smart and fight to get what we want for our people.”

Pariwa thanked Ling-Stuckey for his national leadership and ongoing support for Madang’s development, stating that Ambarina Primary School serves students across the Amron, Baitabag, Riwo, and Nagada communities.

Receiving the funds, Ms Dau commended the provincial leadership for prioritizing education, saying that Pariwa is only the second leader after former Madang Open MP, the late Paul Kamod, to deliver major infrastructure support to the school.

Ambenob LLG president Dum Bal also praised the governor’s focus on education, stating that investment in human capital is vital as suburban growth from nearby Madang town continues to put pressure on local resources.

item.title: Duma urges PNG to embrace modern technology
item.description: State Owned Enterprises Minister William Duma has urged Papua New Guineans to embrace modern technology to ensure the country keeps pace with global advancements. Speaking at the official opening of the new Datec retail showroom in Lae on Friday, Duma praised the company for its long-standing service and commitment to introducing innovative technology into the country.
item.content:encoded:
State Owned Enterprises Minister William Duma has urged Papua New Guineans to embrace modern technology to ensure the country keeps pace with global advancements.

Speaking at the official opening of the new Datec retail showroom in Lae on Friday, Duma praised the company for its long-standing service and commitment to introducing innovative technology into the country.

“We must rise to level with the world,” Duma said.

“Nations are competing through knowledge, innovation, and technology, and we too must remain relevant amid these ever-evolving technological changes.”

Duma emphasized that as the minister responsible for state enterprises, he consistently encourages corporate entities, particularly monopolies and near-monopolies, to remain commercially competitive and customer-focused.

“Their services must be globally relevant, and Datec is a clear example of this,” he said.

Datec PNG chairman Moses Maladina said the firm remains committed to leading the nation's technology sector and expressed strong business confidence in Lae and the Momase region.

Maladina said that rapidly evolving platforms such as Artificial Intelligence [AI] are advancing at an extraordinary pace globally.

“Students, businesses, government agencies, and the private sector accessing Datec services will not be left behind by the remarkable solutions our company offers to ensure everyone remains productive and competitive,” Maladina said.

“The new showroom in Lae demonstrates Datec’s commitment to ensuring the people of Morobe have direct access to the latest technologies, backed by expert technical support and service.”

item.title: Lae church launches reconstruction work two years after disaster
item.description: The Cassowary United Church in Lae, Morobe, has officially launched ground-filling works to reclaim its premises two years after part of its property was destroyed by natural disaster. The church's backyard was washed away by the flooding Bumbu River in August 2024, forcing the congregation to spend two years raising funds to restore the land.
item.content:encoded:
The Cassowary United Church in Lae, Morobe, has officially launched ground-filling works to reclaim its premises two years after part of its property was destroyed by natural disaster.

The church's backyard was washed away by the flooding Bumbu River in August 2024, forcing the congregation to spend two years raising funds to restore the land.

While other centers have celebrated progress, the Cassowary congregation was left to focus on land recovery efforts, ruling out any plans to relocate due to severe land scarcity in Lae.

Speaking during the ground-breaking ceremony, Reverend Rau Vetali expressed deep gratitude to church partners and stakeholders who supported their fundraising drives over the last two years.

“The church conducted two major fundraising dinners, one in Port Moresby and the other here in Lae, and we are still continuing,” Rev Vetali said.

“We are grateful for good support from the provincial administration and the former late Governor Luther Wenge.”

Several business houses in the province have also stepped in to contribute to the backfilling and land reclamation project.

Rev Vetali re-emphasized that the church would not move from its original site, though secondary operations have been shifted out of necessity.

“Land is scarce these days, but we would only source land elsewhere for other church activities,” he said.

“For example, our church-run elementary school has been relocated to a new site at this time.”

The ground-breaking ceremony coincided with a dual celebration marking the church's 57th anniversary alongside United Church congregations across the country.

Meanwhile, backfilling work started last week.

item.title: New Wapulaka Junior High double classroom nears completion
item.description: Construction of a new double classroom at Wapulaka Junior High School in Magarima, Hela, is scheduled for completion later this month. The project fully supported by a K200,000 allocation from the Magarima District Development Authority [DDA], is designed to relieve overcrowded learning spaces and improve conditions for students.
item.content:encoded:
Construction of a new double classroom at Wapulaka Junior High School in Magarima, Hela, is scheduled for completion later this month.

The project fully supported by a K200,000 allocation from the Magarima District Development Authority [DDA], is designed to relieve overcrowded learning spaces and improve conditions for students.

Speaking to NBC News, Magarima DDA chief executive officer Simon Olaija reaffirmed the authority's commitment to advancing local learning facilities.

​"Education remains one of our top priorities," Olaija said. "The K200,000 allocated for this double classroom at Wapulaka Junior High is part of our ongoing effort to upgrade school infrastructure throughout the district." ​ ​He said the project is part of a much broader, long-term initiative. Even prior to recent administrative shifts, when the body functioned as the Komo-Magarima DDA, the authority consistently funded the construction of classrooms and staff housing across the district.

​The CEO also expressed gratitude towards the provincial government for targeting teacher accommodation, a persistent issue that affected teachers.

​"On behalf of the DDA, I want to sincerely thank Hela Governor Philip Undialu for funding vital infrastructure, particularly the 8-in-1 staff housing units," Olaija said.

"Housing has long been a major barrier. Delivering proper living quarters allows our teachers to settle in securely and focus entirely on providing quality education to our students."

​He emphasized that the pioneer Magarima Secondary School continues to receive sustained financial backing from the DDA.

This ongoing support aims to expand facility capacity and modernise resources to accommodate the district's steadily growing student population.

item.title: Three agencies join forces to bring fire service to Hela
item.description: A tripartite Memorandum of Understanding [MOU] has been signed to establish Hela’s first permanent emergency fire response service in Tari.

item.title: Simbu health services scaled down as El Niño affects water and essential supplies
item.description: The Simbu Provincial Health Authority and the Simbu Catholic Health Services have announced a temporary reduction in health services across the province, citing the worsening effects of El Niño on water supply, food security, and other essential resources needed to sustain normal operations.
